title: SELinux Denial Monitoring
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'SELinux Denial Monitoring' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `linux_capacity_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `linux_selinux_denial_monitoring` (UC-1.1.66), SOC dashboard panel "Linux — SELinux Denial Monitoring", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:linux_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=os` sourcetype='syslog' that satisfy the UC-1.1.66 SPL filters for 'SELinux Denial Monitoring'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `os` / `syslog` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `linux_capacity_exceptions.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-1.1.66.

dataSources: `sourcetype=syslog` (or `linux_audit`) carrying SELinux **denied** lines Collected via Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: `Splunk_TA_nix` — Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833)
spl:
index=os sourcetype=syslog (SELinux OR setroubleshoot) denied
| stats count by host, source_context, target_context, object
| where count>5
description: Groups SELinux **denied** log lines by subject/object context so you can see where policy blocks cluster and whether a single tuple suddenly spikes.
value: Policy mistakes and real attacks both show up as **deny** first; a grouped view is faster for app owners to tune booleans and for security to see lateral movement in **context** space.
implementation: If you already ingest **linux_audit** with structured fields, switch the first line to that sourcetype; syslog-only shops should ensure **setroubleshootd** or **auditd** lines actually reach the **os** index. Parse **object** if your build leaves it in `_raw` only.

references.title: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Patch Tuesday / unattended-upgrades** — CPU and disk I/O spike during package application for 'SELinux Denial Monitoring'. Correlate with apt/yum logs in same window.

2. **Nightly backup or log-rotate job** — Predictable I/O burst on fixed cron schedule.

3. **Synthetic monitoring probe** — Nagios/Zabbix agent generates periodic load.

4. **New host onboarding** — Baseline metrics unstable first 48h on `os` `syslog`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `linux_capacity_exceptions.csv` keyed on `host`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Kernel **audit** and SELinux in **enforcing** mode with logging you can read from `/var/log/audit/audit.log` and/or `journalctl` with **SELinux** tags.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
**Props** for **source_context** / **target_context** (or the AVC string equivalents) are critical; use the TA’s add-on for Linux props where possible.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
`action` in `stats` is removed because many builds never extracted it—re-add when your parser supplies it. Start as a **report**; alert after two consecutive windows `>5` for the same tuple.

**CIM** — There is no clean **All_Traffic**-style field for an AVC; keep this on raw unless you also model it into a custom data model.


Step 3 — Validate
`ausearch -m avc` on the host for the same second as Splunk; `sealert` (setroubleshoot) for human-readable text if you use the GUI helper.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Send **deny** spikes to the app that owns the **target** context, not only SOC, when the pattern matches a release.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk_TA_nix` — Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=syslog into os. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`host, object, source_context, target_context`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We help you see when the “extra safety wrapper” on the system keeps saying no, often for the same file or the same app role, so people can fix policy or look for mischief.
